S047-ASNSP_2013_5_12_4_1001_0-prop-3.4.title: Higher order Glaeser inequality in an interval
S047-ASNSP_2013_5_12_4_1001_0-prop-3.4.difficulty_reason: a) 本题的实质要求是证明区间版的高阶 Glaeser 不等式 (3.5)：对 v ∈ C^k((x_0-d,x_0+d))（v 与 v' 都不变号，v^(k) 是 α-Hölder 连续），有 |v'(x_0)|^{k+α} ≤ C(k)·|v(x_0)|^{k+α-1}·max{ Höld_α(v^(k),(x_0-d,x_0+d)), |v'(x_0)|/d^{k+α-1} }，其中 C(k) 只依赖 k。b) 允许引用（作者原文点名）：Lemma 3.3 给出的常数 δ_k；Lemma 3.2 的判据 (3.2) 及其常数 ε_k（用于把「多项式 P 满足 P(0)=1、P'(0)=-1」转成对 A 的下界）；Taylor 展开与 v^(k) 的 α-Hölder 连续性。c) 必须由本证明完成的部分（具体到做法）：①对称性归约到 v≥0、v'≤0，并排除 v'(x_0)=0 与 v(x_0)=0 两个退化情形；②**分两种情形**：Case 1（(|v'(x_0)|/v(x_0))·d ≤ δ_k）直接由 |v'(x_0)| ≤ δ_k d^{-1}v(x_0) 推出 (3.5)，得 C(k) ≥ δ_k^k；③**Case 2（(3.6)：> δ_k）是本证明的真正核心**——先用 Taylor 展开与 Hölder 连续性得到对**一切** δ∈[0,d] 成立的两条不等式（0 ≤ v(x_0+δ) ≤ Σ_{j=0}^{k} v^{(j)}(x_0)/j!·δ^j + H/k!·δ^{k+α}，以及对 v' 的对应式），**再做变量替换 δ := x·v(x_0)·|v'(x_0)|^{-1}** 把它们改写成关于 x 的两条多项式不等式，并由此**自行构造** P(x) 与 A（(3.7)）：P(x) := Σ_{j=0}^{k} v^{(j)}(x_0)/j!·[v(x_0)]^{j-1}/|v'(x_0)|^{j}·x^{j}，A := H/k!·[v(x_0)]^{k+α-1}/|v'(x_0)|^{k+α}；再用 (3.6) 说明替换后的上界大于 δ_k，从而两条不等式至少在 x∈[0,δ_k] 上成立，接着验证 P(0)=1、P'(0)=-1 使 (3.2) 的假设满足，得出 A ≥ ε_k，最终得 C(k) ≥ (ε_k k!)^{-1}。d) 原文定位：印刷页 1011（陈述与 (3.5)、证明前半）至 1012（证明后半与收尾）。

S047-ASNSP_2013_5_12_4_1001_0-prop-3.5.title: Pointwise and weak-L^p bounds for f' under the sign condition on g
S047-ASNSP_2013_5_12_4_1001_0-prop-3.5.difficulty_reason: a) 本题的实质要求是把 Theorem 2.2 所需的两个定量结论组装出来：在区间 (a,b) 上、g(x)·g'(x)≠0 且 |f|^{k+α}=|g| 的条件下，(1) 逐点估计 |f'(x)|^{k+α} ≤ C_1(k)·max{ H, ‖g'‖_∞·[(b−a)/((x−a)(b−x))]^{k+α−1} }（(3.8)）；(2) 弱 L^p 估计 ‖f'‖_{p,w,(a,b)} ≤ C_2(k)·max{ H^{1/(k+α)}(b−a)^{1/p}, ‖g'‖_∞^{1/(k+α)} }（(3.9)），其中 1/p+1/(k+α)=1。b) 允许引用（作者原文点名）：**已证的 Proposition 3.4**（把 v:=g 用到区间 (x_0−d,x_0+d)、d:=min{x_0−a,b−x_0}）；(2.2) 与 (2.5) 的定义；**Lemma 3.1 的 (2)–(4)**（弱 L^p 空间的性质，用于把逐点界提升为弱 L^p 界）。c) 必须由本证明完成的部分（具体到做法）：①取 x_0∈(a,b)、d:=min{x_0−a,b−x_0}，把 (2.2) 与 g 的条件代入 Prop 3.4 得 |f'(x_0)|^{k+α} ≤ |g'(x_0)|^{k+α}/|g(x_0)|^{k+α−1} ≤ C(k)·max{H, |g'(x_0)|/d^{k+α−1}}；②自行证明初等比较 1/d^{k+α−1} ≤ [(b−a)/((x_0−a)(b−x_0))]^{k+α−1}（这一条是把 Prop 3.4 的 d 依赖换成显式 x 依赖的关键），从而得 (3.8)；③把 (3.8) 与 p 的定义 (2.5) 结合，写出 |f'(x)| ≤ [C_1(k)]^{1/(k+α)}·max{ψ_1(x),ψ_2(x)}（ψ_1:=H^{1/(k+α)}，ψ_2:=‖g'‖_∞^{1/(k+α)}·(b−a)^{1/p}/[(x−a)(b−x)]^{1/p}），再用 Lemma 3.1 的 (2)–(4) 把两个 ψ 的弱 L^p 范数算出来，得 (3.9)。d) 原文定位：印刷页 1013（陈述、(3.8)、(3.9) 与整段证明同页）。

(ii) 结果本身是否研究级——是。它在论文摘要里被单列为交付物（"expressing M_m as a Toeplitz+Hankel determinant for the homogeneous sub-critical model in presence of a boundary magnetic field"），是引言要点清单里 "reduce the problem to the analysis of explicit Toeplitz+Hankel determinants, see Theorem 4.4" 指向的那一条，也是随后湿边界相变分析（Remark 4.5、Remark 4.6，以及印刷 2314 页 "Due to Theorem 4.4, the mismatch 2 gamma_0 disappears ..."）唯一的技术依据。

Statement, verbatim: 'Theorem A.4. --- The following identities are fulfilled for all m in N_0: (A.5) M_{m+1}/M_m = D_{2m+2}/D_{2m+1}, M_m = (2/pi)^m * prod_{k=1}^{2m-1} (1 - 1/(4k^2))^{floor(k/2) - m}.' S047-b21-Q1.difficulty_reason: (1) Result level: research-level and self-standing, not bookkeeping. Theorem A.4 is not a step inside the proof of the paper's main theorem; it is an exact identity, M_{m+1}/M_m = D_{2m+2}/D_{2m+1}, tying the boundary magnetization of the critical homogeneous zig-zag half-plane to the full-plane diagonal spin-spin correlation for all m in N_0, and it yields a fully explicit closed formula for M_m (the second half of (A.5)) once Wu's formula (A.4) is known; with Remark A.5's companion identity M_{m+1/2} M_m = sqrt(2) D_{2m+1}, both the even and the odd column magnetizations of the critical model become explicit functions of D_n. The authors state the novelty twice: journal p. 2323, 'This gives a set of exact identities (see Theorem A.4 and Remark A.5) between M_m and diagonal correlations in the full plane which appear to be new', and journal p. 2278, 'Note that we were unable to find neither Theorem A.4 nor the identity (A.7) in the literature.' (Caveat, stated honestly: this novelty claim is the authors' own literature search, which I did not verify independently; it is recorded here because it is the paper's own positioning, not because an author's say-so settles anything.) (2) Decisive step: borne by this proof, by construction rather than by citation. The proof builds the object it needs. It takes the half-plane Kadanoff-Ceva fermion H(-k,s) = X_{[v]}((-k,s)) with the half-plane boundary condition H(0,s) = 2^{-1/2}[H(-1,s-1) + H(-1,s+1)] on the imaginary line; it mirrors H across that line with a factor 2^{-1/2} on the line itself and one global constant, (A.6) V(+/-k,s) := C H(k,s) if k in N, V(0,s) := 2^{-1/2} C H(0,s) if k = 0; it chooses the normalization C := D_{2m+1}/M_m, i.e. precisely the two normalizations that the theorem is about; the mirrored object is then a spinor on the full-plane double cover branching over v and u = (2m+3/2,0), discrete harmonic everywhere except at the branch points, with V(+/-(2m+1),0) = D_{2m+1}, so by the uniqueness established for the full-plane observable it must be X_{[v,u]}; and evaluating the Laplacian at the branch point reads off 1/2 D_{2m+2} = -[Delta V](-2m-1,0) = -C [Delta H](-2m-1,0) = C (1/2) M_{m+1}, which is the ratio identity. Every one of those steps is performed here; no quoted theorem does the work. The imported inputs are the paper's own harmonicity machinery (Proposition 2.2 / Proposition 2.4 and the values (A.1)-(A.2) from p. 2323), the Section 4.1 boundary conditions (4.3)-(4.4), and the optional-stopping uniqueness of bounded harmonic spinors used in Lemma 3.1 and Lemma A.2 - all of them standard tools applied inside the argument, none of them a black box that returns the identity. (3) Self-built construction: yes, and it is the whole trick. The decisive ingredient is not an estimate or a computation but a constructed map - the discrete reflection of the half-plane observable, normalized by a constant C = D_{2m+1}/M_m that is itself the matching between the two normalizations the theorem then relates. The paper flags the manoeuvre explicitly when it introduces the appendix (p. 2323: 'we use a simple Schwarz reflection argument instead of applying our main result, Theorem 1.1, in the spirit of Section 4.3'). Without the correct normalization the reflected spinor does not have the branch values D_{2m+1} and no identity follows; that matching is exactly the piece of mathematical work the proof supplies. This is the pattern the batch rules ask for - a bearer whose proof invents an object (a reflected, renormalized spinor) rather than a statement whose proof says 'by X'. (4) Length and technical complexity: the unit is short but dense - one displayed pair of identities plus a proof occupying about two thirds of a journal page (roughly 25 lines of text and three displays, split across the p. 2325 / p. 2326 break), with one further step handed off ('The explicit formula for M_m easily follows from the explicit formula (A.4) by induction'). The complexity is conceptual, not volumetric: it lives in (a) the double-cover spinor bookkeeping - which objects live on the half-plane cover branching over v and which on the full-plane cover branching over v and u, and why the factor 2^{-1/2} on the imaginary line is the right one - and (b) the normalization match. The dependency is not free either: (A.2), the value [Delta V](+/-n,0) = -1/2 D_{n+1} that is fed into the final display, is itself imported from p. 2323 as 'a straightforward computation similar to the proof of Proposition 2.2' and is never carried out in the paper, so the proof is complete only modulo that auxiliary computation. That is the one respect in which the unit leans on outside work, and it is why the reason for H3 rather than a higher grade rests on criteria (i)-(iii) below and not on self-containedness.
S047-b21-Q1.h3_criterion_note: (i) Decisive step carried by this proof: yes. The identity M_{m+1}/M_m = D_{2m+2}/D_{2m+1} is produced by the reflection construction inside the proof (the reflection, its boundary factor, the choice C := D_{2m+1}/M_m, the identification of the reflected spinor with the full-plane observable X_{[v,u]}, and the final Laplacian evaluation); nothing is delegated to a citation, and the proof deliberately bypasses the paper's own main theorem ('instead of applying our main result, Theorem 1.1'). (ii) Research level: yes. It is a claimed-new exact identity between two classical objects of the critical planar Ising model - the half-plane boundary magnetization and the full-plane diagonal correlation - published in Annales de l'Institut Fourier; together with (A.7) it converts the magnetization into an explicit product formula, and it is the load-bearing content of the appendix's novelty claim. (iii) Not a routine auxiliary step: yes. The unit is a named theorem of the paper with its own payload, not a step inside somebody else's proof, and it cannot be obtained by a local computation or a standard citation: what has to be invented is the reflected object together with the normalization that makes it satisfy the characterising conditions of the full-plane observable. Checked against the batch traps: the paper nowhere says Theorem A.4 is 'essentially the same as [X]' or is included 'for completeness'; the opposite is claimed ('appear to be new'). That is what separates it from Theorem A.3 / Lemma A.2 (explicitly reproduced from [12, Section 3] for self-containedness) and from Theorem 3.6 / Theorem 3.9 (explicitly streamlined proofs of classical results). Honest counter-consideration: Schwarz reflection is a standard move in discrete complex analysis - the paper itself uses it already in Section 4.1, and [27, Appendix A] uses a related idea - so criterion (iii) rests on the fact that the decisive content here is the normalization match and the resulting identity, both produced here and nowhere else, rather than on the novelty of reflection as a technique. A stricter reader could grade the reflection alone as 'standard', but the unit is not a standard lemma applied in passing: it is a theorem whose statement is the identity that the construction exists to produce.

S047-b21-Q3.difficulty_reason: FOUR-ELEMENT ASSESSMENT. (1) RESULT LEVEL: research-level, not a textbook computation. |Z(X)| = 1 asserts that the freely acting part of Sym+(X) is trivial for the exterior of a hyperbolic knot in a lens space that admits a Poincare-homology-sphere filling; combined with Lemma A.3(2) it forces Sym(X) to be 1 or Z/2Z, with a strong involution in the second case, i.e. it is exactly the load-bearing half of Theorem A.1 (printed p. 16), a published symmetry-group dichotomy that answers Question 10(2) raised on p. 5 of the same article. The content is the exclusion of an entire class of symmetries, not a numerical check. (2) DECISIVE STEP: borne by this proof, not delegated. Every citation in it is a tool applied to an object the proof itself creates: [Kojima 1988; Sakai 1991] give hyperbolicity of the drilled manifold, Thurston [1979, Theorem 5.8.2] gives hyperbolic Dehn filling, [Culler et al. 1987] gives the cyclic surgery theorem used as the final contradiction engine, and Lemmas A.3/A.4/A.5/A.6 (in-paper) give the shape of the quotient. The step that actually produces the contradiction -- the exterior X' of the singular set of the quotient orbifold is hyperbolic; fillings of X' along the two cusps corresponding to lens-space fillings remain lens spaces across a whole family of slopes; choosing a slope that makes the remaining cusp hyperbolic yields two non-hyperbolic fillings at distance >= 2, which the cyclic surgery theorem forbids -- is executed here and nowhere else. (3) SELF-BUILT CONSTRUCTION: yes. The proof builds the auxiliary hyperbolic manifold X' = Z_Sigma = Z - N(Sigma), the exterior inside the quotient orbifold of its own singular set, and a two-variable Dehn-surgery calculus on it: X'(alpha, beta) and X'(alpha, beta_1, beta_2), with a '-' convention for the left-unfilled cusp. It then exploits a structural fact special to this fabrication -- the complement of the cores of the orbi-solid tori is a solid torus when Sigma is connected and a thickened torus when Sigma has two components, so that lens-space fillings of the orbi-lens space transfer to lens-space fillings of X' with one cusp left free -- and closes with hyperbolic Dehn filling plus the cyclic surgery theorem. None of these objects appears earlier in the paper or in the cited literature; the orbi-lens-space machinery of [Boileau et al. 2012, section 3] is used only to name the quotient, not to obtain the conclusion. (4) LENGTH AND TECHNICAL COMPLEXITY: the proof occupies about one printed page (pp. 23-24) but runs four cases, each with its own object (a Seifert fibered complement, or a drilled manifold with one or with two boundary tori) and its own filling argument, and it consumes the whole preceding apparatus of the appendix: the definitions of Z(X), primitive curve, distance Delta, orbi-solid torus and orbi-lens space (printed pp. 17-18), Lemma A.3 (proof on pp. 18-20), the cyclic-quotient classification Lemma A.4 (pp. 21-22), Lemma A.5 and Lemma A.6 (p. 22). Its internal syntax -- orbifold fillings, orbi-lens spaces, two-parameter Dehn filling, the distance identity Delta(mu-bar, gamma-bar) = |Z| Delta(mu, gamma) -- has no analogue elsewhere in the 30 pages.
S047-b21-Q3.h3_criterion_note: THE THREE H3 CONDITIONS, CHECKED ONE BY ONE. (i) THE DECISIVE STEP IS BORNE BY THIS PROOF -- PASS: the exclusion of a nontrivial freely acting subgroup of Sym+(X) is carried out in this proof; the appendix's programme lists it as the terminal step (c) ("and ultimately (c) that Z(X) is trivial", printed p. 17), and the proof of Theorem A.1 spends exactly one clause on it: "Then since Z(X) = 1 by Lemma A.7 ...". (ii) THE RESULT IS RESEARCH-LEVEL -- PASS: a symmetry-group dichotomy for hyperbolic knots in a lens space with a Poincare-homology-sphere surgery; it is the published answer to the paper's own Question 10(2) (p. 5) and it is what makes Theorem A.1 a statement in the literature. (iii) NOT A ROUTINE AUXILIARY STEP -- PASS: the proof fabricates its own manifold X' and converts a symmetry question into a two-variable Dehn-filling question; the conclusion cannot be obtained by citing a known theorem, because no known theorem states that the exterior of a knot in a lens space with a P-filling has trivial Z(X). CONSIDERED, EXAMINED AND REJECTED AS H2: the lemma is introduced by the author's sentence "The final lemma needed to establish the theorem can be proved in a similar manner to the lemma above". Per this batch's rules an author's own importance claim is not evidence either way, so the two proofs were compared line by line. A shared skeleton is real (case on the primitivity of gamma-bar; the non-primitive case ends with Lemma A.4 + Lemma A.5 giving a Seifert fibered quotient, contradicting hyperbolicity of X), but Lemma A.6 never leaves the quotient manifold X/Z_f, whereas Lemma A.7's Case 2 builds X' = Z - N(Sigma) and performs two-parameter surgery; the identity Delta(mu-bar, gamma-bar) = |Z| Delta(mu, gamma) >= 2 and the whole of Case 2b occur only here. The 'similar manner' sentence therefore describes a shared case skeleton, not a reused mechanism, and it does not demote the item. ALSO CONSIDERED AND REJECTED AS THE TARGET: Lemma A.3, which carries steps (a) and (b) -- its decisive inference (Sym+(X-tilde) is cyclic or dihedral, Z(X-tilde) is cyclic, [Sym+ : Z] <= 2, the latter only with a strong involution) is imported wholesale from [Boileau et al. 2012, p. 627] and [Neumann and Reid 1992, Proposition 9.1], so under this batch's rule (mechanism entirely off-the-shelf => H2) A.3 is the weaker candidate; Lemma A.7 is where the appendix does work of its own. Other in-paper items rejected on the same ground: Proposition A.2 (a one-paragraph reduction whose engine is the imported cyclic surgery theorem); Lemma A.4 (explicitly "follows from a careful reading of [Dunbar 1988]"); Lemma A.5 (no proof given -- "A simple case analysis shows ..."); Lemma 13 (assembles [Boileau and Otal 1991; Birman and Menasco 1993; Baker 2014a; Giroux 2002; Baker 2014b] and says so: "This can be seen in the spirit of [Baker 2014a]"); Proposition 15, Theorem 7 and Theorem 8 (assemblies of cited theorems); Theorem 14 (Hedden's theorem, quoted); Corollaries 2-3 (one-line consequences of the already-collected Theorem 1). FIDELITY CAVEATS A GRADER SHOULD WEIGH: the printed proof contains at least three dropped-symbol typos, all transcribed verbatim and flagged [sic] -- X'(gamma, -) where the neighbouring sentence writes X'(gamma-bar, -), and X(mu-bar, sigma_n, sigma'_n,m) and X(-, sigma_n, sigma'_n,m) for X'(...) -- and Case 2b is dismissed by the single sentence "This case is nearly identical to the previous" rather than written out; the transcription preserves exactly that asymmetry, so the unit is complete as published but Case 2b's details are not in the paper. The trailing remark after the end-of-proof square prints "Z(M)" where the appendix's notation is Z(X); kept as printed and flagged.

decisions.evidence: 已把本库所有可用的论文头部挖过：aif3604/3605/3607、ASNSP 2013、MSP 305-1、DROPS t5/t12/t30、Lurie。结果：1 条 H3（Lurie Prop 3.4.6）对约 20 条 H2；且委派判定员的 H3 声明连续 6 次被 2/2 复核全盘推翻。
decisions.why_it_matters: 『顺链收承担者』是【找到候选】的好办法，但不提高 H3 率。真正产出过 H3 的只有两处：教材的头部（HoTT 头部 30%）、参考书的节冠名主定理（Stacks）。
decisions.action: 后续把力气放回 Stacks 与（出网后的）新教材/讲义；论文线仅在出网后作补充。

retry_note: DROPS/LIPIcs 早先用『数定理行数』否掉；该量具已被证明会假阴性（在另一篇论文上数出 0，实有 Thm 1.1/4.4）。本次重挖：t1 确为真阴性（特邀报告，无定理环境）；t5/t12/t30 有『定理+紧邻证明』形态 ⇒ 收下 3 条 H2，无确认的 H3。⇒ 『新来源必有 H3 头部红利』这条期望在本块不成立，如实记。
